clue.text: Violet gets excited about the French; she's flighty

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled name goes around the French article
an excited person is stirred up, so the name's letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the name taken as written, as anagram fodder
la is a French word for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A girl called Violet gets worked up over French things, and she is fickle.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the name is split, with LA dropped into the gap after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes a temperament that changes suddenly and unpredictably, the same as a flighty, capricious person.

clue.text: Destructive creatures take against stoat with no tail

indicators.note: an animal with no tail has lost its end, so the word's final letter is cut off

parts.note: v. is the abbreviation for versus, meaning against
ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's view: harmful animals line up against the stoat, whose tail has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermin are pests such as rats and foxes, wild animals regarded as harmful to crops, livestock or property.

clue.text: Find lewd girl, by the sound of her

indicators.note: judging a girl by her sound means listening to the words spoken, not their spelling

parts.note: lewd is low (vulgar) and the girl is Kate; said together they make the verb

explanation.surface: Someone is told to track down a woman of loose morals, known mainly by reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is, so the verb is a direct synonym of find.

clue.text: Row round lakes using steering lever

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the row is wrapped around the lakes

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
L is the abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone rowing a boat around lakes steers with a lever at the stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like the rowing in the scene, but it is the noun meaning a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the bar fixed to a boat's rudder, the handle used to turn it and steer.

clue.text: Lewd girl takes in little man returning with IOU

indicators.note: to take in is to admit inside, so the girl's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the short name is read right to left

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the name Victor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecherous woman entertains a small man coming back, bringing a promissory note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little man' is a shortened man's name rather than a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascivious means feeling or showing obvious sexual desire, so it is a near synonym of lewd.

clue.text: Suppress joint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold back or smother, as a yawn
second meaning: the knee-like joint in the hind leg of a horse or dog

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a vet's term: the joint above a horse's hock.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to smother or restrain; the noun is the anatomical name for a horse's hind-leg joint corresponding to the knee.

clue.text: Wit exercised before light goes at dusk

indicators.note: exercised means put through its paces, worked over, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Humour is put to work just before daylight fades in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light goes at dusk' reads as one phrase, but the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the soft half-light after sunset, the time of evening also called dusk.

clue.text: Insincere praise makes even Terry lose heart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so losing it means the middle letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: flat means even or level
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Being buttered up with false compliments is enough to dishearten even a man named Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like the adverb (even Terry), but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive compliments paid to please or gain favour, praise that is not genuinely meant.

clue.text: Go abroad and point to Russian warplane''s speed

parts.note: E for east, a point of the compass
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave the country and indicate how fast a Russian jet flies.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave your own country to settle permanently in another one overseas.

clue.text: Dare-devil is, reportedly, to destroy not so much

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: to wreck is to destroy; the spelling drops the silent W
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A daredevil is said, by rumour, to break fewer things than you would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Dare-devil used as an adjective describes someone heedless of danger, which is what a rash, careless person is.

clue.text: Salvador takes four to the Festival of Light

indicators.note: the painter takes something in, holding the number inside his name

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The painter Salvador Dali brings four people along to a Hindu festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is split after its first two letters to hold the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali (also Diwali) is the Hindu festival of lamps held in autumn, widely called the Festival of Light.

clue.text: Fearless, I receive the New Testament with false pride

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: false means not true or genuine, so the word's letters are rearranged into a fake form

parts.note: NT is the standard abbreviation for the New Testament
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bold person boasts of accepting the Bible's second part while being proud for the wrong reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means undaunted and brave, showing no fear in the face of danger.

clue.text: Sieve makes mess of trifle

indicators.note: making a mess of something throws it into disorder, so the dessert's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the dessert taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Pushing a trifle through a kitchen sieve would ruin the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered dessert of sponge, custard, fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter, like a sieve, is a device that lets liquid through while holding back solid bits.

clue.text: First aid required after skis become involved in Elf oil spill

indicators.note: becoming involved means getting tangled up, so the skis' letters are mixed in with the rest
a spill scatters its contents everywhere, so the oil phrase is rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the words as printed, but the parse needs an F where the second L stands: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: Skiers crash into a pool of spilt elf oil and someone needs resuscitating.
explanation.walkthrough: The published clue is faulty: the fodder has two Ls and one F, the answer one L and two Fs. The intended mechanism is plainly an anagram of skis with the oil phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, the emergency breathing given to revive someone, is a standard first-aid technique.

clue.text: Reject heir and take Sid back to succeed

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the name is read from right to left

parts.note: the name taken as written
to succeed someone is to inherit their title or estate

explanation.surface: A family drama: cut off the heir and bring Sid back to take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' looks like 'do well', but it means come after and take over.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to deprive an heir of their inheritance, cutting them out of a will.

clue.text: Search through dustbins in South Carolina to retaliate

parts.note: SC is the US postal abbreviation for South Carolina
to avenge is to retaliate for a wrong

explanation.surface: Someone rummages through rubbish bins in South Carolina to get their own back.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to look for usable food or items among waste and discarded rubbish.

clue.text: Keep company with new aid

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
N is the abbreviation for new
to serve is to help or aid

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay with a firm that offers fresh assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve is to preserve or save something from waste or harm, to retain it.

clue.text: Recommend lawyer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb, to speak in favour of a course of action
second meaning: the noun, a barrister who pleads cases in court

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to publicly support or urge; as a noun it is a professional pleader in court, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Obscure rupture causes heavy rainstorm

parts.note: to cloud is to obscure, as in clouding the issue
a burst is a rupture, as in a burst pipe

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note: a hidden internal tear brings on a torrential downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective on the rupture, but it is the verb meaning to darken.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden, very violent fall of rain over a short time.

clue.text: Sleep around and return to abduct

indicators.note: around means on all sides, so the sleep word wraps the other piece

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the little joining word is written backwards

parts.note: the conjunction taken as written

explanation.surface: Sleep around, then come back to carry somebody off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a plain joining word, but it is the piece reversed. Kip is British slang for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to seize and carry them off by force, usually for ransom.

clue.text: Restless person is strangely gifted

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A comment that a restless, twitchy child is oddly talented.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidget is someone who cannot keep still and makes small nervous movements.

clue.text: Spot on church produces discoloration

parts.note: a blot is a spot or stain
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A stain on a church wall leaves a mark of a different colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is an irregular patch of colour on skin or a surface, a mark of discoloration.

clue.text: Far-sightedness, or mirage?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ability to plan wisely for the future
second meaning: something seen that is not really there, an apparition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Far-sightedness' reads like the eye condition, but here it means foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both foresight about the future and a dreamlike image or apparition, which a mirage is.

clue.text: It''s not on: chemical company always missing ways to become authorised

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named letters are taken away from the preceding word

parts.note: something that is off is not on
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, the big British chemicals firm
taken as written
the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that a chemicals firm keeps skipping the proper procedures to get approved.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Official means approved or sanctioned by those in authority, so it is a synonym of authorised.

clue.text: Absolutely not right in a Scandinavian country

indicators.note: in puts the letter for right inside the emphatic refusal

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone insists there is definitely no right of something in a Nordic land.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a kingdom on the western side of the Scandinavian peninsula, alongside Sweden.

clue.text: The witching hour might, taking 1 dn

indicators.note: taking means absorbing, so the word for strength takes the reference inside it

parts.note: taken as written
1 read as the Roman numeral I
taken as written: the abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: The hour of witches might bring along the vermin from 1 down.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 dn' looks like a cross-reference to the vermin at 1 down, but the setter wants it read literally as a numeral and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is traditionally called the witching hour, when witches and ghosts were believed to be abroad.

clue.text: Headless axe embedded in rotten tree in Devon

definitions.note: names the city by where it is rather than what it is

indicators.note: embedded in means fixed inside, so the shortened tool sits within the other letters
rotten wood falls apart, so the tree's letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: headless means without its head, so the first letter of the tool is cut off

parts.note: taken as written, before beheading

explanation.surface: A woodsman's axe has lost its head, stuck in a decaying tree somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; its county town is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the cathedral city and county town of Devon, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Send Des to repair

parts.note: the name taken as written
to patch is to mend or repair

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a man called Des off to fix something.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch (or dispatch) is to send off a letter, parcel or messenger to a destination.
